title: Communication & Influence — Practical Assessment
description: Product Pitch & Persuasive Presentation — a self-recorded one-minute video pitch of an original product, brand or solution.
instructions:
PRODUCT PITCH & PERSUASIVE PRESENTATION

Project: Product Launch Presentation
Category: Communication, Public Speaking & Influence
Presentation Format: Self-recorded Video
Duration: 1 Minute (60 Seconds)

1. PROJECT OVERVIEW

For this assessment, you are required to conceptualise an original product, brand, or innovative solution and present it through a one-minute video pitch.

Imagine you are the founder of a startup introducing a new product to the world. You have the opportunity to stand before a room of potential customers, investors, or stakeholders, and your responsibility is to convince them that what you are presenting is worth their attention.

Your goal is not merely to describe your product. Your goal is to communicate its value, demonstrate why it matters, generate interest, and persuade your audience to take action.

By the end of your presentation, the examiner should understand your product, recognise its value, and feel compelled to either purchase it, join its waitlist, or learn more about it.

2. YOUR TASK

Come up with an original product, service, or brand concept.

It can be something entirely new, an improvement on an existing product, or an innovative solution to an everyday problem.

You have complete creative freedom over what you choose to create.

Once you have developed your concept, prepare a one-minute founder-style presentation introducing and pitching your product.

Your presentation should communicate:
- What your product is.
- The problem it solves or the need it addresses.
- Who the product is designed for.
- Its major features and benefits.
- Why your audience should care about it.
- What makes it worth choosing.

You must conclude with a compelling call to action that encourages your audience to make a decision.

Remember: You are not giving a classroom presentation. You are pitching a product you genuinely want people to buy.

3. PRESENTATION & DELIVERY REQUIREMENTS

Your delivery will be assessed beyond the words you use. We want to see how effectively you use your voice, body language, structure, and presentation techniques to communicate and influence.

A. Tone & Intonation
Pay attention to how you use your voice throughout the presentation.
- Avoid maintaining the same vocal tone from beginning to end.
- Emphasise important words and statements.
- Use vocal variation to communicate excitement, confidence, and conviction.
- Ensure your tone matches the message you are communicating.
- Avoid sounding monotonous or as though you are reading a script.

B. Cadence & Pacing
Your speaking rhythm matters.
- Avoid rushing through your presentation.
- Maintain a comfortable and intentional speaking pace.
- Know when to slow down to emphasise an important point.
- Allow your sentences to flow naturally.
- Avoid unnecessary pauses that interrupt the delivery.

C. Pausing & Emphasis
Learn to use silence as a communication tool.
- Introduce intentional pauses between important statements.
- Pause before or after powerful statements where necessary.
- Give your audience enough time to process important information.
- Avoid filling every silence with unnecessary words such as "um", "uh", and "you know".

A well-placed pause can communicate more confidence than speaking continuously.

D. Structure & Flow
Your presentation should have a clear beginning, middle, and end.
- Open with something that captures attention.
- Introduce the problem or opportunity.
- Present your product as a valuable solution.
- Communicate its benefits convincingly.
- Close with a strong call to action.

Your presentation should feel like one connected conversation, not a collection of unrelated statements.

E. Confidence & Conviction
Present your product as someone who genuinely believes in what they are introducing.
- Maintain confident body language.
- Make appropriate eye contact with the camera.
- Avoid looking down repeatedly to read your script.
- Communicate with clarity and certainty.
- Avoid unnecessary gestures or distracting movements.

Your audience should feel that you understand what you are presenting and believe in its value.

4. PERSUASION & INFLUENCE

This is one of the most important aspects of the assessment.

Your objective is to make the examiner believe that your product is worth buying or investing in.

Do not simply list features. Explain the value behind those features.

For example, instead of merely saying what a product does, communicate how it makes someone's life easier, solves a problem, saves time, or creates a better experience.

Understand the difference between describing a product and selling the value of a product.

Your communication should:
- Connect with the audience's needs.
- Make the problem easy to understand.
- Present the solution in a convincing manner.
- Communicate benefits rather than simply listing features.
- Build interest and anticipation.
- Create a reason for the audience to take action.

The goal is to make your audience understand the value of your product so clearly that taking action feels like a natural decision.

This is persuasion through clarity, value, and effective communication, not manipulation.

5. RESEARCH & PREPARATION

Before recording your presentation, conduct research on effective product pitches, founder presentations, and professional public speaking.

You are encouraged to watch YouTube videos featuring:
- Startup founders pitching their products.
- Product launch presentations.
- TEDx presentations.
- Professional keynote speakers.
- Successful entrepreneurs introducing new products.

Pay attention to how these individuals:
- Open their presentations.
- Introduce problems and solutions.
- Use vocal variation.
- Control their speaking pace.
- Incorporate pauses.
- Emphasise important statements.
- Maintain audience engagement.
- Close their presentations.

Do not just watch these presentations. Study the techniques and understand why they work. Use your research to improve your own delivery.

6. VIDEO RECORDING REQUIREMENTS

Your submission must be a video recording of yourself delivering the presentation.

Please observe the following:
- Your face and upper body must be clearly visible.
- Record in a well-lit environment.
- Ensure that your audio is clear and audible.
- Position your camera properly.
- Maintain eye contact with the camera.
- Avoid distracting backgrounds or unnecessary movements.
- Do not use background music that competes with your voice.
- Ensure that your presentation is delivered naturally and confidently.

Presentation duration: 60 seconds maximum.

You may prepare a script or presentation outline beforehand, but your delivery should not feel like you are reading directly from a written document.

7. ASSESSMENT CRITERIA

Your presentation will be evaluated based on the following:

- Tone & Intonation: 15
- Cadence & Pacing: 15
- Pausing & Emphasis: 10
- Structure & Organisation: 15
- Confidence & Body Language: 15
- Persuasion & Influencing Ability: 20
- Clarity & Audience Connection: 10
- TOTAL: 100

8. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS

Submit the following:
1. Name of your product or brand.
2. A brief description of what your product does.
3. Your recorded one-minute product pitch.

Video duration: 60 seconds maximum.

Because a video is too large to upload, submit your recording as a link (Google Drive, Dropbox, YouTube unlisted or similar) and set the sharing so the academy can view it. Use the response box below for your product name and a brief description of what it does.

9. FINAL INSTRUCTIONS

Before recording, ensure that:
- Your product concept is clearly defined.
- You understand the problem your product solves.
- Your presentation has a compelling opening.
- Your message is structured and easy to follow.
- Your delivery has intentional tone variations.
- Your pacing is controlled.
- You make effective use of pauses.
- Your body language communicates confidence.
- Your presentation communicates value and builds conviction.
- Your closing CTA gives the audience a clear reason to act.

10. UNDERSTANDING THE PURPOSE OF THIS ASSESSMENT

Communication and influence go beyond speaking good English, using sophisticated vocabulary, or knowing how to construct grammatically correct sentences.

True communication is the ability to transfer an idea from your mind into someone else's understanding in a way that makes the message clear, meaningful, and actionable.

Influence is the ability to communicate that idea so effectively that it shapes how people think, what they believe, and the decisions they make.

You could have an excellent product, a brilliant idea, or a solution that genuinely solves a problem. But if you cannot communicate its value effectively, people may never understand why they need it.

This assessment is designed to test your ability to bridge that gap.

We want to see how well you can take an idea, communicate its value, connect with an audience, and influence a decision within just 60 seconds.

You have one minute. Make it count.

Good luck!
